details:
Space Doc - Health Monitor is a web app that helps astronauts assess their own health on long missions, and helps researchers monitor study participants. In Self-check, the astronaut chooses their environment (spacecraft, space station, rover, or planetary or lunar base) and activity (sleeping, resting, exercising, or other), then enters heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, temperature, sleep and mood. Each reading is colour coded Normal, Watch or Alert, with plain guidance on how to measure it, why spaceflight affects it, and what to do next. A clickable body map, trend charts of saved readings and a suggested daily and weekly routine support the habit. The Participant and All participants views use NASA bed rest study data on cardiovascular fitness and immune markers, and automatically flag when someone drifts from their own baseline or from the group. The aim is earlier detection of health problems when medical help is far away. It is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript only, with no server, and the data was prepared with Python.
Tools and software used
Canva: interface designing
Claude AI: coding and debugging
Gemini AI: understanding and cleaning data
ChatGPT: debugging and modifying code

Languages: Python
